rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Faraday's laws are the exchange rate between electricity and matter. The **first law** — mass proportional to charge (m = ZIt, with the electrochemical equivalent Z = E/96500) — turns amperes and seconds into grams: 2 A for 30 minutes through AgNO₃ is 3600 C, 0.0373 faradays, **4.03 g of silver**.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Q = I × t (t in seconds) - First law: m = ZIt, Z = E/96500 - Second law: m₁/m₂ = E₁/E₂ - Moles of electrons = Q/96500 - Gas at STP: V = (22.4/n) × (Q/96500) L

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Z and E are different numbers:** Z is per coulomb (mg/C), E is per faraday (g/F = equivalent mass); m = ZIt and m = (E × Q)/96500 are the same formula written twice.  ·  **Deposited vs liberated:** metals deposit as atoms (mass directly); gases liberate as molecules — use 22.4/n litres per faraday, not 22.4.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The mass of a substance deposited at an electrode is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed; and for the same quantity of electricity through different electrolytes, the masses deposited are proportional to their equivalent masses."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The copper coulometer*** — weigh a copper cathode before and after, divide the gain by 0.329 mg/C, and you have measured the charge without a single electronic meter.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: electrolysis, quantitative aspect, faraday's laws of electrolysis (within Oxidation and Reduction).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Weighing Electricity Faraday's two laws (1833) turn coulombs into grams: the mass deposited at an electrode is proportional to the charge passed (first law) and, for the same charge through different electrolytes, proportional to the equivalent mass (second law).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Faraday's first law - **Statement:** the mass of a substance deposited (or liberated) at an electrode is **directly proportional to the quantity of charge** passed through the electrolyte. - **m ∝ Q**; Q = I × t (current in amperes × time in seconds), so **m = Z × I × t**.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Pipeline: Q = It → /96500 → × E. Seconds check before anything. Series shortcut: masses ∝ E. Gas per F: H₂ 11.2 L, O₂ 5.6 L, Cl₂ 11.2 L. Cu²⁺ 2F/mol, Al³⁺ 3F/mol, Ag⁺ 1F/mol.

rows.text: Quote both laws verbatim before the calculation — the statement carries marks. Keep 96500 symbolic until the final line; premature rounding compounds errors in multi-step numericals.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Faraday's constant is the meeting point of electrochemistry and the mole: 96500 C moves one mole of electrons, so charge ÷ 96500 = moles of electrons — the same conversion that powers cell potential calculations in later units.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: First law: m ∝ Q, m = ZIt, Z = E/96500. Second law: same Q through series electrolytes → m₁/m₂ = E₁/E₂; 1 F deposits 1 equivalent. F = 96500 C = 1 mol electrons. E values: Ag 108, Cu 31.75, Al 9. Numericals: 2 A × 30 min Ag → 4.03 g; 5.4 g Ag ⇒ 1.59 g Cu in series; 0.2 F → 1.12 L O₂, 2.24 L H₂ at STP.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Every aluminium smelter is a Faraday's-law calculator: ~13–15 kWh per kilogram of Al follows directly from 3 × 96500 C per 9 g — electricity prices set metal prices.

rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): A current of 2 A is passed through acidulated water for 9650 s. Calculate the volume of oxygen liberated at the anode at STP (F = 96500 C).** — Charge passed: Q = I × t = 2 × 9650 = 19300 C. Faradays: 19300/96500 = **0.2 F**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Value | |---|---|---| | **Faraday's first law** | m ∝ Q passed | m = ZIt | | **Faraday's second law** | Same Q: m ∝ E | m₁/m₂ = E₁/E₂ | | **Electrochemical equivalent (Z)** | Mass per coulomb | Ag: 1.118 mg/C | | **Faraday constant** | Charge of 1 mol electrons | 96500 C | | **Equivalent mass (E)** | Formula mass / n |…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why one faraday deposits one equivalent - Every mole of electrons carries 96500 C; an ion of charge n needs n electrons per ion, so 1 mol electrons (1 F) reduces exactly 1/n mol — that is, **one equivalent** — of the ion. The second law is this sentence restated: equal charge → equal equivalents → masses in the ratio of equivalent masses.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **One faraday's harvest (1 F = 96500 C)** | Ion | Half-reaction | Deposited per F | |---|---|---| | Ag⁺ | Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag | 108 g Ag | | Cu²⁺ | Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu | 31.75 g Cu | | Al³⁺ | Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al | 9 g Al | | H⁺ | 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂ | 11.2 L H₂ (STP) | | OH⁻ | 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ | 5.6 L O₂ (STP) | **The two laws at a glance** | Basis | First law |…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Derive the second law from the first law using the concept of the equivalent.  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  Limit to remember: force on moving charge f = q(v×b); on a wire f = bil sinθ.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Time must be seconds:** I × t with minutes or hours silently multiplies errors by 60 or 3600 — convert first, always.  ·  **n is the ion's charge, not the element's valence in the compound:** Cu²⁺ → 2F per mole even though "copper sulphate" mentions no charge; Al³⁺ → 3F.  ·  **First law needs one cell; second law needs several:** mixing them up in numericals produces ratio errors — check what the question actually varies.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (3m): State Faraday's first law and calculate the mass of silver deposited when a current of 2 A passes through AgNO₃ solution for 30 minutes.** — First law: the mass deposited at an electrode is directly proportional to the quantity of charge passed, m = ZIt.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): The same current passes through two cells in series containing AgNO₃ and CuSO₄. If 5.4 g of silver deposits, what mass of copper deposits?** — By Faraday's second law, m(Ag)/m(Cu) = E(Ag)/E(Cu). E(Ag) = 108 (n = 1); E(Cu) = 63.5/2 = 31.75 (n = 2). **m(Cu) = 5.4 × 31.75/108 = 1.59 g.**  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Calculate the volume of oxygen liberated at STP when a current of 2 A passes through acidulated water for 9650 s.** — Q = 2 × 9650 = 19300 C = 0.2 F. Oxygen: 4e⁻ per O₂, so 1 F gives 5.6 L; 0.2 F gives **1.12 L of O₂ at STP** (and 2.24 L of H₂ at the cathode).
